justification: Changes which houses are shown which DCP rules. The route change stops 2,827 unkeyed precinct rules reaching every house without a precinct; the gate rule, once applied with the user's yes, stops 913 Marrickville Part 8 heritage rules reaching non-heritage houses. A mistake would hide rules from houses they cover or keep showing them to houses they do not, silently.

pre_impl.existing_data: Measured on production 2026-10-15: 2,827 served rules with v2_dcp_layer 'precinct', v2_precinct_id NULL and zones ALL (canterbury_bankstown 1,953, ku_ring_gai 858, parramatta 16). Marrickville part8-heritage: 1,361 served rules, all generic layer, none with v2_marker 'heritage'; 913 have a non-heritage topic, 448 topic 'heritage'. Hand-checked address audit (30 addresses, 300 rules): 49 severe, 42 of them rules for another area; 24 are unkeyed precinct rules, 6 Part 8 rules on non-heritage lots.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: chapter_scope recorded Part 8 as whole_council although its own sentence (p15) names heritage items and HCAs. The _ALL_HERITAGE pattern did not match its wording, so it would have been counted as a named-area chapter. The 448 topic-heritage Part 8 rules were hidden not only from non-heritage houses but from every HCA house too, because queryHeritageByHca reads v2_marker only.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Reuses GATE_RULES (re-run by dcp_commit_approved.py after every publish) and the existing DQ-143/146 probes; the route change removes a branch rather than adding one. The existing precinct warning still tells the user precinct controls may exist.
pre_impl.external_source_error: No external call. The Part 8 sentence was read from the council PDF in R2 (part8-heritage.pdf p15, quote_check found).
pre_impl.frontend_type: queryLayer returns [] for the precinct layer when no precinct_id is sent, the same type as an empty result.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: Before: silent wrong answer (a centre or site rule shown at a house outside it). After: the rule is missing at houses inside its precinct until the precinct is keyed, and the page's existing precinct warning says site-specific controls may exist. Counted by DQ-146 (reopened, 2,945).

falsifiable_check.command: cd frontend-nextjs && npx jest __tests__/api/precinct-layer-fail-closed.test.ts ; cd .. && python -m pytest tests/test_gate_rules.py tests/test_chapter_scope_probes.py -q
falsifiable_check.fails_when: The jest test fails if the route queries the precinct layer for an address without a precinct, or queries unkeyed rows when a precinct is given. The pytest tests fail if the Part 8 sentence stops matching _ALL_HERITAGE, if Part 8 is not a heritage_general chapter in DQ-143, if the gate rule is missing, or if the probes stop mirroring the route.
falsifiable_check.observed_red: With route.ts restored from origin/main the new jest test fails 1 of 2 (the no-precinct case). The first regex edit did not apply (string mismatch) and was redone.

functions.name: queryLayer (precinct branch)
functions.input: the layer name 'precinct' plus the property filters, including an optional comma-separated precinct_id
functions.output: Rules keyed to the given precinct ids; [] when no precinct id is given
functions.if_none: No precinct id returns [] before any query; the precinct warning is computed separately.

values.what: served precinct-layer rules with no precinct key
values.source: SELECT count(*) FROM regulatory_provisions WHERE served set AND v2_dcp_layer='precinct' AND v2_precinct_id IS NULL AND zones ALL

values.what: DQ-146 / DQ-143 / DQ-144 with the new definitions, before the Part 8 write

queries.purpose: Precinct layer rows for the property's precinct only.
queries.where_clause: v2_is_actionable AND is_current AND v2_dcp_layer = 'precinct' AND source_council = $ AND (v2_precinct_id = ANY($) OR v2_precinct_id = 'PART_G_OVERVIEW')
is_current = true AND source_council = 'marrickville' AND source_chapter_key = 'part8-heritage'

break_it.scenario: A house inside a C-B or Ku-ring-gai centre whose rules are unkeyed.
break_it.what_happens: It no longer sees those centre rules until their precinct is keyed.
break_it.how: Accepted by the user (2026-10-15): missing is better than wrong. The precinct warning still shows; DQ-146 counts every hidden rule until it is keyed.

break_it.scenario: An HCA-specific Part 8 statement (e.g. Enmore-Newtown) with v2_heritage_hca NULL.
break_it.what_happens: Shown to every HCA house in Marrickville, not only its own HCA.
break_it.how: Recorded limit; the heritage_general gate does not compare areas (DQ-143 scope note). Next step: key Part 8 statements of significance to their HCA.

break_it.scenario: A house that is only an archaeological site or Aboriginal heritage place.
break_it.what_happens: That house is not shown the Part 8 heritage rules at all.
break_it.how: No land layer for those; recorded in the gate rule comment and the chapter_scope note.

break_it.scenario: A precinct_id is sent but names no keyed precinct (locality fallback ids).
break_it.what_happens: The precinct layer query returns no rows for that house.
break_it.how: Unchanged by this PR: that branch never returned unkeyed rows, and the route's precinct warning (case 2: ids match zero precinct provisions) still fires.

break_it.scenario: Marrickville Part 8 is re-published and the new rows arrive without the heritage marker.
break_it.what_happens: Part 8 rules would reach every Marrickville house again, heritage or not.
break_it.how: marrickville_part8_heritage is a GATE_RULES entry, which dcp_commit_approved.py re-runs for the council after every publish; DQ-143 counts any Part 8 row left untagged.

post_merge.db_reset: Yes, with the user's yes: python scripts/derive_precinct_keys.py --council marrickville --only marrickville_part8_heritage --apply (1,361 rows get v2_marker 'heritage'; backup in data/db_rollback_backups).
